reviewers: assistant:claude-opus-5 — analytical reviewer for the declared-only policy study. Not a recruiter, not a second human rater, and not the matcher.
review.methodology: Every verdict was written by reading the profile fixture and the posting as two documents and deciding what a careful hiring reviewer would conclude, using the verdict definitions and reviewer rules fixed in matching_real_v1/README.md. Each rationale was written at the same time as its verdict. The whole file was completed and frozen before the matcher was executed against this dataset even once; the profiles and postings were authored first, and the only property of the engine consulted while writing them was the curated technology vocabulary, so that a case would test declared-only policy rather than vocabulary coverage. Where the two reviewer rules that govern declared-only evidence (rule 1, stated years and project technologies count as corroboration; rule 6, duration counts paid employment) point in different directions, the verdict follows the rule that governs the requirement's own kind and the conflict is recorded in contested_note rather than resolved silently.
review.independence_statement: No verdict in this file was read off, derived from, or adjusted to any matcher output. The expectations were authored and the file frozen before the first execution of any algorithm against declared_only_v1, and the SHA-256 of this file at that moment is recorded in the analysis that accompanies the dataset. Where the matcher later disagreed, the disagreement is the measurement: no verdict here has been edited because an algorithm reached a different one.

ground_truth.contested_note: The posting asks for 'any Terraform exposure', which is the lowest bar a posting can set, and a skills-list entry is an assertion of exactly that much. A second reader could hold that a graduate's list entry does not establish even exposure, in which case this is UNCERTAIN like the Kubernetes line above. The verdict turns entirely on the posting's wording, not on the strength of the evidence, which is identical in both rows.

ground_truth.contested_note: The second role says the scheduling layer was migrated onto Celery, and Celery requires a broker that is very often Redis. A reader willing to follow that inference would call this MATCHED. The reviewer here would not: the document names Celery, not its broker, and the profile could equally be describing RabbitMQ or SQS. This is the clearest case in the dataset where a human's verdict depends on entailment from described work — something no deterministic rule in this codebase computes.

The verdict follows rule 6 because the requirement is a duration requirement, and the conflict is recorded rather than resolved.
